name: Abdul Jabbar
role: Language Movement martyr and civilian participant
contribution: Abdul Jabbar came to Dhaka with his family for his mother-in-law's medical treatment and joined the public protest around Dhaka Medical College on 21 February 1952. He was fatally wounded when police opened fire on demonstrators.
context: He was not a university student leader but an ordinary visitor who entered the Language Movement's defining confrontation as students and members of the public gathered to demand recognition for Bangla as a state language of Pakistan.
impact: Jabbar's death became part of the martyr memory that gave the Language Movement a lasting moral and civic vocabulary. His story also broadens the movement's social history beyond campus activism to include members of the public who joined the demonstrations.
highlight: A civilian participant remembered among the martyrs of the 21 February 1952 Language Movement protest.
seoTitle: Abdul Jabbar: Language Movement Martyr of 1952
seoDescription: Learn about Abdul Jabbar, the civilian participant who was fatally wounded during the 21 February 1952 Language Movement protest in Dhaka.
shortAnswer: Abdul Jabbar was a civilian participant in the 1952 Language Movement who was fatally wounded during police firing in Dhaka.

faq.question: Who was Abdul Jabbar?
faq.answer: He was a civilian who came to Dhaka for a family medical emergency and joined the 21 February 1952 Language Movement protest, where he was fatally wounded by police fire.

faq.question: Why is Abdul Jabbar remembered?
faq.answer: He is remembered as one of the Language Movement martyrs whose death became part of the public memory and annual commemoration of 21 February.
